# #9 — feat: add upsert_person / add_person tool for structured contact management

## Problem

The `find_person` tool exists but there's no way to CREATE or UPDATE people records programmatically. Currently the only workaround is logging freeform `log_thought` entries with person tags, which is messy and doesn't leverage the people table schema properly.

## Proposed Solution

Add the following tools:

### `upsert_person`
Create or update a person record with structured fields:
- `name` (required)
- `email`
- `phone`
- `imessage` / `apple_id`
- `relationship` (e.g. owner, friend, colleague, family)
- `notes`
- `tags`

### `update_person`
Update specific fields on an existing person by ID or name.

### `delete_person` / `archive_person`
Soft-delete a person record (consistent with `archive_entry`).

## Why

Agents need a proper address book. Right now contacts get scattered across `log_thought` entries which:
- Can't be queried structurally (only semantically)
- Don't enforce schema (easy to miss fields)
- Pollute the thoughts table with contact data

## Current Workaround

```bash
mcp2cli open-brain log_thought --params '{"content": "PERSON: Jackie Rojas...", "tags": ["person:jackie", "address-book"]}'
```

This works but is a hack.

## Related

- `find_person` tool already exists (read-only)
- People table presumably already has schema -- just needs write access exposed

### Direction taken and why — PR #10 body

> ## Summary
>
> Closes #9
>
> - **New `upsert_person` tool** -- creates or updates people by name using `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (person_name) DO UPDATE`. Omitted fields preserve existing values via COALESCE. Embeds `name + context + notes` on every write.
> - **Migration 004** -- extends `relationships` table with `email`, `phone`, `relationship_type`, and `metadata JSONB` for extensible contact info (apple_id, imessage, social handles).
> - **Agent role upgraded** from read-only to read-write on relationships, so agents can manage contacts.
> - **`find_person` and `update_entry` updated** to support the new columns.
>
> No separate `update_person` or `archive_person` tools -- `update_entry` (by ID) and `archive_entry` (soft-delete) already cover those cases for all tables including relationships.
